body: encountering same issue within recent v13.1.1 version

i've been encountering this as well. seems to be caused by this change https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/lib/typescript/writeConfigurationDefaults.ts#L169 to include the build dir in the tsconfig types.

with Nx it adds `../../dist/apps/blahblah` which causes a bunch of module not found errors when validating typescript.

i've "fixed" this locally by just commenting out the writing to tsconfig in my node_modules so i could continue working without disabling ts typechecking: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/lib/typescript/writeConfigurationDefaults.ts#L222
If you don't want to update your node_modules, you can add the wrong include in the exclude array. It is still just a workaround though.

Same, more specifically i get these messages
```sh
info  - Checking validity of types ..We detected TypeScript in your project and reconfigured your tsconfig.json file for you. Strict-mode is set to false by default.

The following suggested values were added to your tsconfig.json. These values can be changed to fit your project's needs:

        - include was updated to add '../../dist/apps/peer-review/.next/types/**/*.ts'
```

Then i get the error

```sh
info  - Checking validity of types ..Failed to compile.

Type error: Cannot find module '../../../../../app/[pr]/page' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

because `dist/apps/peer-review/.next/types/app/[pr]/page' has this as the first line
```ts
import * as entry from '../../../app/[pr]/page'
```

which obviously doesn't have types.

I used the workaround @Sylphide  suggested to fix this.

EDIT: the console notifies you of making these changes every single time you start the dev server or try to build the project btw, probably has something to do with is

Encountering the same issue with Nx. According to my testing it **started from version 13.1.0**. 

It was quite a frustrating experience as undoing my last changes (including reverting back to 13.0.x) still had my builds failing so I spent some time trying to fix the code I wrote. Turned out the issue was not written by me but by Next modifying configuration files. 😬👀 Therefore, I'll write a friendly warning just in case:

**Please note that the order of testing different Next versions here is important as during a build Next adds new include paths to the `tsconfig.json` file, but does not remove entries added by other Next versions. If you want to switch between Next versions multiple times and get authentic results then you have to remove any `**/.next/types/**` entries manually before trying to build with a different version.**

The same issue after 13.1.0 Nx + NextJS - can't build 
`Cannot find module '../../../../app/layout' or its corresponding type declarations.`

I hope there will be some progress on this issue 🙏

Same issue here with Next `13.1.1`

The "exclude" workaround works for me:

```
  "include": [
    /* ... */
    "../../../apps/your-project/.next/types/**/*.ts",
    "../../../dist/apps/your-project/.next/types/**/*.ts"
  ],
  "exclude": [
    /* ... */
    "../../../apps/your-project/.next/types/**/*.ts",
    "../../../dist/apps/your-project/.next/types/**/*.ts"
  ]
```

NextJS should not modify the `tsconfig.json` files at any time. A warning or suggestion to add at build/serve time is fine,  it should have a `-silent` option. 

It has been ages since I've had a framework modify configuration files past the initialization in setup. This is really making Next v13 and the app directory unusable.

### Is anyone working on a PR? I'm happy to look into a fix if not??
Yep, can confirm this is the exact thing I've just experienced. New to NX, and this is a pretty bad first experience.

Will try using the exclude hack that everyone else has been using.
